<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Sudan]]
****[[South Sudan]] Vice President [[Riek Machar]] confirms the country's first case of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. The patient is a 29-year-old woman who had arrived from [[Ethiopia]] in February and is now in isolation. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-southsudan/south-sudan-confirms-first-case-of-coronavirus-idUSKBN21N0EA (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]]
****Former [[Prime Minister of Libya|Libyan Prime Minister]] [[Mahmoud Jibril]] dies in [[Egypt]] from COVID-19 at the age of 67. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-04-05/former-libya-premier-jibril-dies-in-cairo-from-coronavirus (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ethiopia]]
****The [[government of Ethiopia|government]] confirms its first death from COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-ethiopia/ethiopia-reports-its-first-death-of-a-covid-19-patient-idUSKBN21N0IE (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco]]
****King [[Mohammed VI of Morocco]] pardons 5,654 prisoners and orders new measures to protect inmates from COVID-19. The prisoners were selected on the basis of their age, frail health, time spent in prison and good conduct. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20200405-morocco-to-release-5654-prisoners-amid-coronavirus-outbreak/ (Middle East Monitor)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic on USS Theodore Roosevelt|COVID-19 pandemic on USS ''Theodore Roosevelt'']]
*****[[United States Navy]] Captain [[Brett Crozier]], recently relieved of his command of the [[aircraft carrier]] [[USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71)|USS ''Theodore Roosevelt'']] after his letter pleading for aid for the coronavirus outbreak aboard his ship was leaked to the press, tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/04/05/magazine/navy-captain-crozier-positive-coronavirus.html (''The New York Times'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
*****[[New York (state)|New York]] reports 8,327 new confirmed cases and 594 more deaths from COVID-19, bringing the state's death toll to 4,159 and 122,000 cases, according to Governor [[Andrew Cuomo]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-usa-new-york/new-york-state-reports-594-coronavirus-deaths-in-past-24-hours-idUKKBN21N0ND (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Haiti]]
****[[Haiti]] reports the country's first death from COVID-19, a 55-year-old man with underlying health conditions. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200405-haiti-reports-its-first-coronavirus-death (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] is admitted to hospital 10 days after testing positive for COVID-19. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-52177125 (BBC News)]
****Queen [[Elizabeth II]] gives an [[List of addresses to the nation by the British monarch|address to the nation]], just the fifth such event in the monarch's  68-year reign, where she compares social isolation to the world war evacuations, thanks the public for their resilience and the world for unifying. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-52176222 (BBC News)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
*****[[Scotland]]'s [[Chief_Medical_Officer_(United_Kingdom)#Chief_Medical_Officers_for_Scotland|Chief Medical Officer]] [[Catherine Calderwood]] resigns after breaking her own rules on COVID-19 restrictions by visiting her second home in [[Elie and Earlsferry]]. She had been warned by [[Police Scotland|police]] about her conduct. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-scotland-resignati/scotlands-chief-medical-officer-resigns-after-flouting-own-coronavirus-guidance-idUKKBN21N0WH (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*Five people are killed in a [[mass shooting]] in [[Yelatma]], [[Ryazan Oblast]], [[Russia]]. The suspect has been arrested and said he shot dead four men and one woman for "talking too loudly". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-52173341 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malawi]]
****[[President of Malawi|President]] [[Peter Mutharika]] announces a stimulus package to alleviate the economic stress resulting from the disease. To help finance this program, he and all [[government of Malawi|government]] ministers are taking a ten percent wage cut for three months. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-52172164 (BBC News)]

;Science and technology
*[[Misinformation related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[YouTube]] says it will remove videos promoting a [[conspiracy theory]] linking [[5G]] to COVID-19, while "borderline content" will be removed from search results. The decision comes after four more [[mobile phone mast]]s are [[arson|set on fire]], and [[broadband]] engineers have received threats, in several UK cities. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/apr/05/youtube-to-suppress-content-spreading-coronavirus-5g-conspiracy-theory (''The Guardian'')]
